questions.prompt: Which structure does classic BFS use for the frontier?
questions.explain: A queue keeps the order fair: first discovered, first explored.

questions.prompt: On an unweighted graph, the first time BFS visits a node is:
options: The fewest edges from the start
questions.explain: BFS expands one hop at a time, so the first visit is shortest in hops.

questions.prompt: Why do we keep a visited set?
options: To avoid revisiting nodes and infinite loops on cycles
questions.explain: Without visited, cycles send you around forever.
